preheader: 51 non-fiction books reviewed in the British papers this week, one line each.

books.author: Darren Loucaides
books.subject: Business & power
books.line: Investigation into Pavel Durov, the elusive Russian founder of Telegram, and the rebel image that drew a billion users.
books.why: A secretive living founder at the centre of a story still unfolding.

books.author: Andrew Hankinson
books.subject: True crime
books.line: Reconstructs the felling of the Sycamore Gap tree, setting the overlooked, hard-up lives of those behind it against the nation's grief.
books.why: A crime the whole country followed; this tells the side nobody heard.

books.book: No One Tells You: The Last Years of Edna O'Brien
books.author: Carlo Gébler
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: O'Brien's son on his mother's long final decline - an intimate family biography.

books.author: Simon Sebag Montefiore
books.subject: History
books.line: Sweeping history of how the modern Middle East was forged from its cultures, creeds and rivalries.

books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: Paired review of two books arguing a threatened, fragmenting EU can still pull together.

books.author: Liz Truss
books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: The former prime minister's own account of her time in power, read sceptically.

books.author: Luiz Schwarcz
books.subject: Books & writing
books.line: A leading Brazilian publisher on why books feel like living companions, an idea with very old roots.

books.author: Gideon Rachman
books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: The FT's foreign affairs commentator weighs how close the world now is to a third world war.

books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: Life of the shape-shifting actor, from the National to Dumbledore, that leaves his habit of invention largely unsolved.

books.book: Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?
books.author: Judi Dench
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: Dench on directors, ageing and her dislike of being treated as a national monument.

books.author: Kim Ghattas
books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: The 1984 assassination of Malcolm Kerr in Beirut, and how it set the course of US-Iran enmity.
books.why: One killing that unlocks a 40-year geopolitical story. Three papers reviewed it.

books.book: The Stay Behinds: Sweden's Cold War Guardians
